summary: **Parties Present:** Ms. Swapna Seshadri, Advocate, NHPC Ms. Ranjitha Ramachandran, Advocate, CTUIL Shri Aneesh Bajaj, Advocate, CTUIL The present petition has been filed by NHPC Limited (hereinafter referred to as ‘Petitioner’) regarding the wrongful levy of transmission deviation charges on the injection of infirm power from the 800 MW Parbati-II HEP (“Parbati-II Project”) under the CERC (Sharing of Inter-State Transmission Charges and Losses) Regulations, 2020 (hereinafter referred to as 2020 Sharing Regulations) and its Amendments. The Petitioner has made the following Prayers: - _(d) In the interim, direct NRPC/CTUIL not to take any coercive action(s) against the Petitioner during the pendency of the present Petition;_ - _(e) Pass such orders as deemed fit and necessary in the facts and circumstances of the present case._ _“Learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the present Petition has been filed seeking quashing of the bill dated 27.12.2024 raised by Respondent No.1, CTUIL, on the Petitioner for an amount of Rs. 276,312,036/- and also for seeking a declaration that transmission deviation charges are not applicable on injection of infirm power prior to the COD of the Petitioner’s 800 MW (4x200 MW) Parbati-II HE Project, and consequently for_ _2. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission directed as under:_ _(b) The Petitioner to implead National Load Despatch Centre (NLDC) as a party to the Petition and to file a revised memo of Parties within a week._ _(c) The Respondents to file their respective replies, if any, within six weeks with a copy to the Petitioner, who may file its rejoinder within four weeks thereafter._ _(d) The Petitioner to file the following information/ clarifications on an affidavit within four weeks:_ - _(ii) Clarification as to whether the Petitioner has paid the transmission charges against RTDA on injection of such infirm power, which was scheduled in the Power market or not._ ** Submission of the Petitioner in compliance with RoP for hearing dated 21.05.2025: ** - (h) The Petitioner, while challenging the principle of the transmission deviation, has not raised any dispute on the computation of the amount in the said RTDAs or Invoices. Further, the Petitioner has referred to the entire amount of Rs. 27.63 crore in its prayers, whereas the challenge in the Petition pertains only to the injection of the infirm power. - (i) As on date, the Petitioner has not paid any amount against the said bill. Petitioner is required to pay the entire amount, including a late payment surcharge, and CTUIL reserves the right to take appropriate action for the non-payment. **7.** The Petitioner, in its rejoinder vide affidavit dated 17.09.2025, to the reply filed by the CTUIL, reiterated its earlier submission and mainly submitted as under: **8.** The Petitioner and the Respondent, CTUIL, made detailed submissions and concluded their respective arguments. The Commission permitted both sides to file their respective written submissions and reserved the matter for order. **9.** Petitioner in its written submissions dated 25.02.2026 mainly reiterated its earlier submissions and mainly submitted as under: - (c) CTUIL has contended that NHPC has not challenged RTDAs issued by NRPC and is only challenging the Disputed Bill. This contention of CTUIL is wrong and misleading. NHPC has already demonstrated at the 49th Commercial SubCommittee Meeting dated 11.03.2024 that no charge or liability can be imposed without a positive provision to that effect. - (d) Petitioner has sought to rely on the First Amendment and draft First Amendment along with the Explanatory Memorandum. The issue must be decided in accordance with the applicable Sharing Regulations, not on the basis of the Explanatory Memorandum or Draft Regulations issued thereafter. **15.** We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner and Respondent and the documents placed on record. The following issue arises for our consideration: **20.** In view of the above, as the Petitioner did not have any open access during the disputed period, in terms of Regulation 12(1)(a) of the 2020 Sharing Regulations, the infirm power injected by the Petitioner is liable for payment of transmission deviation charges. **23.** Petitioner has also contended that NRPC was uncertain about the applicability of deviation charges on infirm power, which is evident from the Minutes of the 49 th NRPC Commercial Sub-Committee Meeting dated 11.03.2024, as well as NRPC’s letter dated 12.08.2024, vide which NRPC sought clarifications from the Commission. The relevant extract of the NRPC letter dated 12.08.2024 is as under: of the Petitioner’s project. Accordingly, the Petitioner's prayer to quash the Bill dated 27.12.2024 issued by CTUIL for Rs. 27.63 crore on account of transmission deviation charges is rejected. We direct the Petitioner to make the payment against the said bill, along with the applicable late payment surcharge as per LPS Rules, within a period of 15 days of the issuance of this Order.
title: Petition under Section 79 (1) (A) and (F) of the Electricity Act, 2003, read with relevant provisions of the CERC (Sharing of Inter-state Transmission Charges and Losses) Regulations, 2020 and amendments thereof regarding wrongful levy of transmission deviation charges on injection of infirm power from Parbati-II HEP 800 MW Project. NHPC Limited
